title: The Idea
coreMove: Let people act near the facts while using short communication checks to keep the system aligned.
sourcePressure: The source contrasts Katrina with Wal-Mart to show the difference between trapped central response and decentralized local execution connected by disciplined communication.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version praises decentralization as freedom. The real move is local action plus a tight signal structure.

sourceAnchors.name: Katrina
sourceAnchors.detail: The source sidecar identifies Katrina as the contrast case for a central response structure that could not move authority and signal fast enough.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Katrina shows what happens when the field keeps waiting for a center that cannot see fast enough.

sourceAnchors.name: Wal-Mart local response during Katrina
sourceAnchors.detail: The source sidecar contrasts Wal-Mart with Katrina as a system where local actors had more room to respond close to facts on the ground.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Wal-Mart matters here because local action did not mean silence; it meant action with a usable signal back to the system.

hook: The people closest to the problem should decide
tryThisNow: Ask your team what they need
examples: same construction coordination shell as ch03

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person 'You' direct address, retrospective 'It took her three weeks to see', question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.domain: Megan, a flood relief supply hub coordinator
exampleSpecs.audience: disaster volunteers deciding what can be local and what must be shared
exampleSpecs.stakes: neighborhood shelters wait for diapers and insulin coolers while the central desk tries to approve every load
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Megan gives shelter leads authority to reroute essentials but requires a two-line status update before each truck leaves
exampleSpecs.firstImage: cardboard softening under rainwater at the loading dock

exampleSpecs.domain: Marco, an airport ground delay operations lead
exampleSpecs.audience: transport coordinators balancing local gates and network consequences
exampleSpecs.stakes: gate crews improvise aircraft moves that strand wheelchairs and baggage if nobody shares the signal
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Marco authorizes gate agents to swap two stands locally, then requires the wheelchair desk and baggage lead to confirm the move in one shared channel
exampleSpecs.firstImage: At 6:18 a.m., Marco sees three delayed flights blinking amber on the ramp board

exampleSpecs.domain: Frida, a rural ambulance mutual-aid dispatcher
exampleSpecs.audience: emergency coordinators who cannot run every call from one desk
exampleSpecs.stakes: two towns have ambulances moving toward the same crash while a dialysis call goes uncovered
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Frida lets field crews choose the closest unit but makes each crew state destination, coverage gap, and next available time over the radio
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "Say the gap before you roll," Frida says into the headset

exampleSpecs.domain: Nicolas, a hotel evacuation desk manager
exampleSpecs.audience: hospitality leaders handling a smoke alarm across departments
exampleSpecs.stakes: housekeeping, security, and front desk each act quickly but leave one stairwell unchecked
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Nicolas redesigns the alarm response so each floor captain can clear rooms locally but must call in stairwell status and guest count
exampleSpecs.firstImage: It took Nicolas one false alarm to see the missing stairwell was a communication failure

exampleSpecs.domain: Aanya, a community kitchen meal-surge organizer
exampleSpecs.audience: nonprofit teams serving a sudden influx without formal hierarchy
exampleSpecs.stakes: allergy meals and hot trays drift apart when volunteers solve local problems silently
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Aanya assigns local station decisions but makes each station move a colored magnet when allergy stock, hot trays, or drivers change
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You hear the foil lids crackle while three vans idle outside the kitchen door

exampleSpecs.domain: Henrik, a wildfire animal shelter intake lead
exampleSpecs.audience: temporary shelter teams matching fast local care with shared records
exampleSpecs.stakes: animals are fed and medicated locally but owners cannot be reunited if tags and cage moves vanish
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Henrik allows each aisle team to move animals for safety but requires every move to hit the intake photo board within two minutes
exampleSpecs.firstImage: How do you move fast without losing the animal someone is searching for?

tryThisNowSpec: For one active workflow, name one decision that should move closer to the facts and the one signal that must come back when it moves.

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
